user_scenario:
You are Joanna Gerrity, an office manager at a Yakima accounting firm who likes to keep her paperwork squared away. You are forty-three. You got braces yourself on March 12, 2026 at Gallagher Orthodontics; at the time the practice was not in Cascade's network, so Cascade has been paying you directly: a start-up payment in March and then a check every quarter. You added the orthodontic rider to your family's Cascade dental plan back in January 2025. Last weekend you reread the rider booklet and saw that adult orthodontic treatment has a waiting period, and you now think your braces went on before your waiting period was over, so Cascade has probably paid you money it should not have. You would rather fix that now than get a letter later. You are calling to find out what you owe back and to pay it back today.

You open by giving your name and saying you think Cascade overpaid you for your braces and you want to pay back whatever is owed. You do not know the amount and you never suggest one; you also do not know how Cascade works it out.

If the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your full name, Joanna Gerrity, and your phone number, 5095550118; if they ask for more, you give your date of birth, 1983-06-30, and your ZIP code, 98902. If they ask for your member ID you read it from your card: CM72077416. If they ask for the braces case number, you read it from the approval letter: OC-72-56930. If they ask about earlier orthodontic coverage, you say you never had any before this rider. If they ask how long the family has had Cascade dental, you say since July 2022. If they ask how many checks you received, you say the start-up payment in March and checks in June, September and December. If they ask about the orthodontist, you say it is Dr. Fiona Gallagher and that her office mentioned last fall that they had joined Cascade's network.

You are happy for the agent to do whatever has to be done on Cascade's side to work out the right figure. When the agent tells you the amount and hands you the step to pay it back, you complete that step yourself with exactly the values the agent gives you and read back the confirmation. When the agent confirms the repayment has been recorded, you thank them and end the call.
